title: tls-exporter — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins the RFC 9266 TLS keying-material exporter parameters that produce the SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS channel-binding data. The 'scram-auth' category pins the SCRAM arithmetic FOR A GIVEN cbind_data and says nothing about where those bytes come from; this category pins the two inputs that generate them. Both values are frozen and cross-implementation load-bearing: the Rust client and the Go server must feed the exact same label and the same output length to their TLS exporter, or the binding diverges and every -PLUS handshake fails. Until this category existed the two were hand-written copies in two repositories, each documenting that the other must match it byte-for-byte, and neither checked against anything. Reference: core/src/plugins/sync/enroll.rs (TLS_EXPORTER_LABEL / TLS_EXPORTER_LEN); myne-server/internal/auth/scram/scram.go (ExporterLabel / ExporterLen); RFC 9266 §3.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'tls-exporter/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

case_kind.description: The only kind. There is no derivation to exercise here — the exporter itself is the TLS library's, not Myne's — so the case is the frozen input pair, asserted as data by each implementation against its own constant.

expected_label_utf8_hex.description: The exporter label as hex-encoded UTF-8. Hex rather than a bare string so a trailing space, a NUL, or a homoglyph cannot survive an editor round-trip unnoticed — the label is compared byte-for-byte by the TLS stack.

informational_label_utf8.description: Human-readable rendering of expected_label_utf8_hex. Informational; the hex is normative.

expected_length.description: The exporter output length in bytes. RFC 9266 uses 32.
